verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena mānadinno gahapati ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
verses.english: Now at that time the householder Mānadinna was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

verses.pali: Atha kho mānadinno gahapati aññataraṁ purisaṁ āmantesi:

verses.english: “Please, my friend, go to Venerable Ānanda …” …

verses.pali: na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ na yāpanīyaṁ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamoti.
verses.english: “Sir, I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. The pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.

verses.pali: Evarūpāya cāhaṁ, bhante, dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno kāye kāyānupassī viharāmi ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
verses.english: When I experience such painful feelings I meditate observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
I meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharāmi ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Yāni cimāni, bhante, bhagavatā pañcorambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni desitāni, nāhaṁ, bhante, tesaṁ kiñci attani appahīnaṁ samanupassāmī”ti.
verses.english: And of the five lower fetters taught by the Buddha, I don’t see any that I haven’t given up.”
You have declared the fruit of non-return.”
